item.title: Operator of plane in Miami crash had prior safety complaints by former employees
item.description: The Amazon Prime Air Boeing 767 cargo plane that crashed off a Miami runway​ on Sunday, killing five people, was operated by a North Carolina company that has been accused by past employees of violating safety regulations, legal documents reveal.

item.title: How much will a $200,000 home equity loan cost per month if opened this September?
item.description: Thinking of taking out a $200,000 home equity loan this September? Here's what the monthly payments could look like.

item.description: Savers looking to grow their money in the next few years should consider the returns a $100,000 3-year CD offers now.

item.title: Remains found 49 years ago in North Carolina identified as teen runaway
item.description: Skeletal remains found in North Carolina in 1977 have been identified as those of Cindy Marcell Blizzard, a 15-year-old girl who ran away from her home in Monkton, Maryland, investigators said.

item.title: Victims identified in deadly plane crash at Miami International Airport
item.description: The Amazon cargo plane crashed off the end of a runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday, leaving five people dead and five others injured.

item.description: President Trump threatened to ban Bombardier sales in the U.S. as Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect. Here's what to know about the aircraft maker.

item.title: 2 savings accounts to consider if the Fed raises rates this September (and one to avoid)
item.description: Not every savings account will be well-positioned to take advantage of a potential Fed rate hike later this month.

item.title: Inside the push to lower voting age to 16 for local elections
item.description: A growing movement across the U.S. is pushing to lower the voting age to 16 for local elections. CBS News correspondent Natalie Brand visited a couple of the cities that have already taken the step to see how it's working.

item.title: Price of crude oil nears $100 a barrel as U.S.-Iran stalemate continues
item.description: Oil prices are rising steadily with no end in sight to the U.S.-Iran standoff impeding tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: What's a good annuity rate in 2026?
item.description: The right annuity could lock in attractive returns for retirement, but not every high-paying option is a good deal.

item.title: College swap shop helps students and families save money and the environment
item.description: For college students, the cost of heading back to campus can add up fast. But at New York University, students are stocking up without spending a dime. CBS News' Evyn Moon reports on how their campus swap is saving students money and giving old dorm gear a new life.

item.title: Dangerous Hurricane Lowell passing just west of Hawaii
item.description: Hurricane Lowell was skirting western Hawaii, bringing damaging winds, heavy rain and punishing waves, the National Hurricane Center said.

item.title: 4 found dead after Miami family's small plane goes missing off Bahamas
item.description: A small plane carrying four family members flying back home to Florida went missing off the Bahamas, the U.S. Coast Guard and authorities in the Bahamas said.

item.title: Elizabeth Holmes doc is "wildest documentary I've ever seen," Vanity Fair correspondent says
item.description: Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's new documentary about Elizabeth Holmes is "probably the wildest documentary I've ever seen," according to Rebecca Ford, Vanity Fair's senior Hollywood correspondent, who was there for the documentary's secret premiere. Ford joined CBS News with more details.

item.title: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to allow use of citizenship database
item.description: The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to intervene in a lawsuit over the use of a controversial data system to review state voter rolls.

item.title: Drone activity at U.S.-Mexico border drops sharply after laser weapon use, Pentagon says
item.description: The U.S. military's use of a laser weapon to shoot down drones led to a nearly 75% drop in the aircrafts' activity at the U.S.-Mexico border, according to the Pentagon. CBS News' Eleanor Watson has more.

item.title: Museum to return remains of 39 people taken during colonial rule in India
item.description: The Pitt Rivers Museum, one of the world's leading institutions for anthropology, ethnology and archaeology, holds over 6,000 artifacts from the Naga community in India.

item.title: Woman who prosecutors say followed Lindsay Clancy's case closely is in court for toddler's death
item.description: An Illinois woman is in court on Tuesday after being charged with murdering her 2-year-old son. Prosecutors say she was heavily invested in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial. CBS News Chicago's Darius Johnson has more. (Warning: This video may contain violent and disturbing content. Viewer discretion is advised.)

item.title: Patrick Clancy's lawyer warns "there will be consequences" for conspiracy theorists
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's ex-husband, Patrick, is responding after conspiracy theorists claimed he was involved in his children's deaths. In a statement Tuesday, his lawyer warned about consequences for those involved. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul has more.

item.title: Goldman Sachs warns oil prices could hit $120 as U.S. fuel costs surge
item.description: Higher gas and diesel prices have cost Americans an additional $100 billion since the Iran war began, according to a Brown University tracker.

item.description: Abraham Altamar was on the phone with his wife when he briefly spoke with one of the pilots of the Amazon cargo plane that overran a runway in Miami.

item.description: New York City officials released thousands of previously unseen documents questioning the air quality at Ground Zero following the 9/11 attacks.

item.description: Most Americans say they're opposed to data centers. But a lucky few have gotten rich selling their land to data center developers.

item.title: Lithuania training civilians to defend against a Russian invasion
item.description: Lithuania is teaching civilians young and old to help defend their tiny nation from a hypothetical Russian invasion, and telling Putin, "We don't fear you."

item.title: France investigates removal of female Eiffel Tower staff for Hindu group's visit
item.description: The mayor of Paris announced an investigation into why female staff at the Eiffel Tower were taken off duty for a visit from a Hindu religious group.

item.title: An iconic photo of the new 60 Minutes team in Murrow's old hangout
item.description: Famed photographer Mark Seliger captured the season 59 team at New York City's Oyster Bar in Grand Central Station.

item.title: U.S. Air Force officer rescued from Iran speaks for the first time to 60 Minutes
item.description: After a U.S. warplane was shot down over Iran, the Air Force and American special forces rescued the two-man crew in one of the largest and most complex rescue operations in U.S. military history. For the 59th season premiere of 60 Minutes, correspondent Norah O'Donnell interviews the weapon systems officer who spent two days on the ground in Iran. In his first public account of what happened, the colonel describes surviving a harrowing ejection and being injured, how he evaded Iranian forces and what he said to his rescuers when they arrived.

item.title: 25 years after 9/11, Taliban rules Afghanistan again, but with U.S. firepower
item.description: CBS News finds Taliban forces patrolling Kabul in American armored vehicles, wearing American tactical gear and carrying American weapons.

item.title: NTSB arrives at MIA to begin investigation into deadly plane crash
item.description: An Amazon cargo plane overran a runway at Miami International Airport and struck several vehicles, killing at least five people and injuring five others, officials said.
